summary: Private/VPC: intermittent DNS resolution failures causing sporadic request timeouts to Redwood Private endpoints
description:
Issue summary
- Customer on Redwood Private (Kubernetes in customer VPC) reports intermittent DNS resolution failures for Redwood service endpoints. Failures manifest as sporadic timeouts / connection errors from workloads calling inference + control plane APIs.

Impact
- Intermittent spikes of failed requests (customer reported ~0.5%–3% of calls during bursts; higher during node scaling events).
- Customer impact is user-facing due to timeouts in their application tier.
- No indication this is affecting Hosted; appears isolated to customer VPC/private networking.

Customer environment / topology (sanitized)
- Deployment mode: Redwood Private in customer-managed Kubernetes cluster.
- Networking: private subnets across 2 AZs; outbound egress through NAT; internal resolution uses VPC DNS + CoreDNS.
- DNS path (as described by customer): app pods -> CoreDNS (kube-system) -> upstream forwarders (VPC resolver / custom forwarders) -> (conditional forward for internal zones).
- Customer uses split-horizon DNS for internal domains; they recently introduced a DNS firewall policy and new forwarders (exact vendor withheld by customer; shared in call).

Symptoms / error examples (sanitized)
- From application logs:
  - "dial tcp: lookup api.<redacted>.redwood-private.local on 169.254.xx.xx:53: i/o timeout"
  - "Temporary failure in name resolution" (varies by runtime)
- From pod exec:
  - "nslookup inference.<redacted>.redwood-private.local" intermittently times out.
  - Success rate improves when retrying immediately.

Frequency / timing notes
- Customer reports incidents during peak traffic windows and when cluster autoscaling adds nodes.
- Symptoms are worse on newly added nodes for ~5–15 minutes after join (hypothesis: resolver/iptables or node-local caching not warm; upstream saturation).

Steps to reproduce (customer)
1) Generate sustained inference traffic (spiky RPS) from application pods.
2) During node scale-out, observe error spikes.
3) Run repeated DNS lookups from affected nodes; observe intermittent timeouts.

Support triage checklist (performed)
- Confirmed request IDs not consistently available due to failures occurring pre-request (DNS failure before HTTP).
- Confirmed failures occur across multiple Redwood service hostnames (inference + control plane), indicating DNS layer rather than a single service.
- Asked customer to collect:
  - CoreDNS ConfigMap (kube-system), CoreDNS logs during spike window
  - Node /etc/resolv.conf for affected nodes
  - Upstream DNS forwarder IPs + timeout policy (sanitized acceptable)
  - Any recent network policy / DNS firewall changes

Initial hypotheses
- Upstream resolver saturation or dropped UDP/53 leading to intermittent timeouts.
- CoreDNS concurrency/forwarding limits too low for traffic bursts; missing cache; aggressive ndots/search causing extra queries.
- NodeLocal DNSCache not enabled; kube-dns becomes a bottleneck during scale events.
- DNS firewall/conditional forwarding intermittently blocking internal zone resolution or causing retries.

Customer-safe mitigations recommended (no Redwood code changes)
1) Enable NodeLocal DNSCache (recommended for high-QPS clusters) and confirm kubelet is configured accordingly.
2) CoreDNS tuning:
   - Ensure "cache" plugin enabled with reasonable TTLs.
   - Increase forward plugin concurrency ("max_concurrent") if upstream supports it.
   - Increase CoreDNS replicas and set anti-affinity across AZs.
3) Resolver tuning on nodes/pods:
   - Reduce excessive search/ndots if causing lookup amplification.
   - Confirm timeout/attempts are not overly aggressive.
4) Network validation:
   - Verify security groups/NACLs allow UDP+TCP 53 to upstream resolvers.
   - Confirm DNS firewall policies allow the Redwood private zones.

Escalation rules (per refreshed playbook)
- P1 / Sev2 escalation criteria for Private DNS failures:
  - Error rate >1% for >10 minutes OR customer reports user-facing timeouts with no stable workaround.
  - Any evidence of cross-customer blast radius (not expected for Private; if suspected, route to SRE).
- When criteria met:
  - Start Slack bridge in #support using bridge template; include: customer, tier=private, region, exact failing hostnames, timing window, CoreDNS status, node count changes.
  - Page Private Deployments / Platform on-call for Private networking issues; loop in SRE only if we suspect platform-wide dependencies or need incident comms alignment.

Requested next actions
- Customer to provide CoreDNS config/log bundle + confirmation of NodeLocal DNSCache.
- Support to draft a short internal troubleshooting snippet/macro for Private DNS failures once confirmed (candidate for known-issues sprint if recurring).

resolution:
Resolved via customer-side DNS hardening:
- Enabled CoreDNS cache and increased CoreDNS replicas/resources.
- Enabled NodeLocal DNSCache to reduce kube-dns bottleneck and stabilize lookups during traffic bursts and node scale-out.

Follow-ups
- Support to add a macro/snippet for Private DNS failures (what to collect, recommended mitigations, and when to escalate).
- If recurrence is observed across multiple Private customers, propose a short known-issues entry (internal-facing) with a customer-safe checklist.
